sentences.text: What if the witch pouring this poison is secretly sorry?
This is Circe Invidiosa, painted by John William Waterhouse in 1892.
Everyone knows Circe from Ovid as the jealous witch who made a monster.
Glaucus loved Scylla instead of her, so she poisoned Scylla's pool.
And the picture seems to agree.
Green poison pours from her bowl, and dark shapes already swirl below.
According to the critic Chris Woods, Waterhouse did not paint his Circe as wholly evil.
Here she becomes a tragic figure who cannot help what she is doing.
She's a woman watching her own jealousy work.
So is she a cruel witch, or a woman who cannot stop herself?

meta.title: The witch who poured her poison with regret
meta.description: Circe Invidiosa was painted by John William Waterhouse in 1892 and is in the Art Gallery of South Australia. Following Ovid, Circe poisons Scylla's pool out of jealousy; the critic Chris Woods sees her here as a tragic figure who regrets what she is doing.
meta.question: A cruel witch, or a woman who cannot stop herself?

sources.claim: Circe Invidiosa is a painting by John William Waterhouse completed in 1892.

Under her feet, Scylla's "barking shapes" already swirl in the bubbling depths below; the transformation is well underway.
Rather, the power of Circe's grave face and tangible jealousy rules this scene, as the vivid colors swirl all around her figure.
